question: Which Linux companion app direction should OpenClaw pursue now that Windows Hub is shipped: the C/GTK app, the Rust/GTK alternative, another external/community app path, or deferral?
rationale: The remaining work is a new platform app with auth, pairing, gateway control, packaging, and supply-chain implications, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product and ownership direction.

options.title: Make C/GTK Primary
options.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/59859 as the primary Linux track because it matches the GTK-native direction and has explicit distro-packaged dependency rationale, while treating alternatives as reference material.

options.title: Choose Rust/GTK Alternative
options.body: Evaluate https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/61576 as the primary Linux direction if maintainers prefer Rust ownership and its gateway-client split over the C/GTK approach.

options.title: Defer Linux Companion
options.body: Keep Linux on CLI, Gateway, and web surfaces for now, close or pause broad app PRs, and reopen only after a sponsored platform-app plan exists.

recommendation.title: Make C/GTK Primary
recommendation.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/59859 as the primary Linux track because it matches the GTK-native direction and has explicit distro-packaged dependency rationale, while treating alternatives as reference material.

likelyOwner.reason: He opened the umbrella issue, set the GTK-native Linux direction in discussion, and has the strongest companion-app feature-history signal.
